items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is the knight retreat to f3 (depth 16).
One black piece attacks the knight.
The retreat to c2 is rated at least a quarter-pawn below the best move.
Ndb5 is rated at least four pawns below the best move.

hints: Which of your pieces is attacked, and by what?
Where can the knight go and still attack something? Look at e5.
Nf3 attacks the e5 pawn and keeps the knight in the game.
items.explain: The e5 pawn attacks the knight on d4. Nf3 keeps the knight active: it now attacks the e5 pawn, defended only by the knight on g6. The retreat to c2 is passive, and Ndb5 walks into ...a6, after which the knight is short of safe squares; the engine at depth 16 rates it at least four pawns below Nf3.

feedback_by_move.d4c2: Nc2 saves the knight but looks at nothing; the engine at depth 16 rates it at least a quarter-pawn below Nf3.
feedback_by_move.d4b5: Ndb5 leaves the knight with few squares: after ...a6 it is in trouble. The engine at depth 16 rates it at least four pawns below Nf3.

items.prompt: Black to move, after 20...Bxf3+ 21.gxf3. Which side owns the bishop pair, and what does it cost that side?

answer.class: White, at the price of doubled f-pawns
options: White, at the price of doubled f-pawns
White, at the price of a pawn
Black, at the price of doubled f-pawns

claims.statement: Only White owns both a light and a dark bishop.
White's f-pawns are doubled.

hints: Count each side's bishops, then look at the f-file.
Black has one bishop and two knights. How did White's pawns recapture on f3?
White has two bishops, and the g-pawn recaptured on f3.
items.explain: White has the bishops on b2 (dark) and b3 (light); Black has one bishop (on f8) and two knights. The doubled f-pawns are White's price for the pair.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is Nb5 (depth 16).
After Nb5 two white pieces attack the bishop on d6.
Ba4 is rated at least a quarter-pawn below Nb5.
Before the knight move one white piece, the rook on d1, already attacks the bishop on d6.

hints: Which black piece stands on a square White's pieces can attack twice?
Look at the bishop on d6 and the d-file behind it.
Nb5 attacks d6, a7 and c7, and it uncovers the bishop on b2.
items.explain: Nb5 attacks the bishop on d6 as a second attacker: the rook on d1 already looks at d6, and the knight adds to it. The move also takes the knight off the long diagonal, so the bishop on b2 now aims at e5. Black defends d6 twice, so nothing is won at once, but Black must now deal with a7 and c7 as well.

feedback_by_move.b3a4: Ba4 pins nothing and leaves d6 alone; the engine at depth 16 rates it at least a quarter-pawn below Nb5.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is a6 (depth 16).
After a6 one black piece, the pawn, attacks the knight.
Rd7, the game move, is rated at least 0.6 pawns below a6.

hints: Can you attack the attacker?
The knight has no pawn-proof square near. A pawn move hits it.
a6 kicks the knight with tempo.
items.explain: ...a6 attacks the knight, so White must act at once; the engine still prefers White slightly. Rd7 defends d6 a third time but leaves e5 and g6 to White's bishops; at depth 16 the engine rates it at least 0.6 pawns below a6.

feedback_by_move.d8d7: Rd7 is the game move. It adds a defender, but White's bishop swings to c2 with threats; the engine at depth 16 rates it at least 0.6 pawns below a6.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is Bf5 (depth 16).
After Bf5 one white piece attacks the rook on d7.
f4 is rated at least 1.5 pawns below Bf5.
After Bf5 Rd8 the engine at depth 16 rates White at least three pawns better.
After Bf5 Rb7 the engine at depth 16 rates White at least three pawns better.
After Bf5 Rc7 the engine at depth 16 rates White at least three pawns better.

hints: Which black piece is only defended by the king?
Look for a move that attacks the rook on d7 with a bishop.
Bf5 attacks the rook; the knight on b5 already attacks the bishop on d6 and a7.
items.explain: Bf5 attacks the rook on d7, which only the king defends. The rook cannot simply step away: from d7 it guards d6 and a7, and the knight, the bishops and the other rook already aim at those squares and at e5. Black is overloaded, so wherever the rook goes he loses a piece or a pawn. At depth 16 the validator finds White at least three pawns ahead after Rd8, Rb7 and Rc7. f4 is rated at least 1.5 pawns lower.

feedback_by_move.f3f4: f4 attacks e5 but lets Black untangle; at depth 16 the engine rates it at least 1.5 pawns below Bf5.

items.prompt: White to move. The game is already won; one move collects a loose pawn. Find it.

claims.statement: The engine's best move is Rxe5 (depth 16).
The pawn on e5 is Black's only loose piece.
Bb2 is rated at least 0.4 pawns below Rxe5.
At depth 16 the position before 46.Rxe5 is rated at least three pawns in White's favour.

hints: List which black pieces are attacked.
Which of them has no defender?
The pawn on e5 is attacked by the rook and no black piece defends it.
items.explain: The rook on c5 attacks e5 and nothing defends the pawn. Taking it gains a pawn at no cost. The position is already winning (the engine rates it at least three pawns for White), so this is a closing step, not a hard choice; the quiet Bb2 is at least 0.4 pawns lower.

feedback_by_move.c1b2: Bb2 improves the bishop but leaves the pawn on e5 for Black to protect; at depth 16 the engine rates it at least 0.4 pawns below Rxe5.
